title: api-gateway: streaming routing, proxy buffer tuning, and OpenAI-compat fixes
author: Marcus Nguyen
description: Context: Production traffic has surfaced intermittent streaming failures and degraded tail latency when requests are routed across region/fallback policies. Separately, OpenAI-compat users reported truncated streaming payloads when using function/tool-calling and structured output flows. Motivation: Reduce streaming tail latency, prevent proxy-induced truncation, and keep the OpenAI compatibility layer behavior unchanged for existing clients while allowing larger structured outputs. This PR makes three focused changes: 1) smarter routing policy for streaming requests that prioritizes warm downstream proxies and region affinity to reduce cold-start tail. 2) tuning and bounds for the streaming proxy read/write buffer sizes and backpressure semantics to avoid interior truncation of chunked frames. 3) OpenAI-compat fixes for streaming function/tool calling and structured output framing (preserve chunk boundaries, content-type passthrough, and explicit final delimiter). Changes (high level): - routing: add a weighting heuristic in router that scores endpoints by last-active timestamp, current inflight, and model-compatibility tag; small config flag (routing.stream_affinity_enabled) to gate behavior. - proxy buffer/backpressure: increase default read buffer from 64KB -> 256KB, write buffer to 512KB with an upper bound configurable by env; switch to length-prefixed chunk handling for internal proxy framing to avoid ambiguous newline-only boundaries. - openai-compat: ensure function-calling JSON blobs emitted during streaming are emitted as complete frames (atomic frame flush), include content-type header passthrough so downstream tools that rely on application/json receive correct headers, and add an explicit "[DONE]" final chunk for legacy clients. - tests and metrics: add integration e2e that simulates routing fallbacks with synthetic cold upstreams; add additional unit tests for function-calling stream framing; emit new metrics (stream.proxy_chunk_retries, routing.stream_affinity_hit) and dashboards. Backwards compatibility: routing change is behind config flag off by default; OpenAI-compat emits the explicit final delimiter only for compatibility mode; buffer upper bounds default to conservative values. Checklist: - [x] Add routing heuristic + config flag - [x] Increase proxy buffer defaults and add env override - [x] Fix OpenAI streaming frame semantics for function/tool calling - [x] Add unit + integration tests - [x] Add metrics and dashboard changes - [x] Update docs (openai-compat streaming notes) Commits summary: - feat(api-gateway): add stream affinity scoring in router - feat(proxy): length-prefixed chunk framing and buffer config - fix(openai-compat): atomic flush for function-calling frames + final delimiter - test: streaming e2e for fallback/routing scenarios - docs: openai-compat streaming behavior and buffer tuning Notes: The routing heuristic deliberately avoids hard routing rules to prevent breaking canaries; it biases routing to warm/low-inflight endpoints which reduced measured p95 tail by ~18% in load tests. Buffer increases addressed several reproduction cases where 64KB split a JSON function payload across chunks and downstream parser dropped invalid partial frames. The explicit final delimiter is only applied when openai_compat_mode=true to avoid surprising new clients. Related: ENG-4123 (routing), ENG-4210 (proxy stability), SUP-8812 (customer report).

feat(proxy): length-prefixed chunk framing and buffer size config
fix(openai-compat): atomic streaming flush for function calling
test(streaming): e2e fallback + cold upstream simulation

review_conversation: Priya Shah: Can we get a short reasoning doc for the buffer defaults? 64->256KB is a big change for memory-constrained proxies.

Marcus Nguyen (author): Agreed — I added defaults.yaml comments and an env override (PROXY_MAX_BUFFER_BYTES) and added a note to docs/openai-compat.md explaining tradeoffs. Memory overhead observed ~+1.2MB per proxy in our standard docker image at peak; still within our pod resource limits in dedicated clusters.

Avery Cole: Routing scoring looks fine but we should ensure it doesn't conflict with capacity-based autoscaler. Suggest emitting routing.stream_affinity_hit so autoscaler can consider affinity separately.
Marcus Nguyen: Added routing.stream_affinity_hit metric and a small metric tag for autoscaler integration. Also validated in a staging run that autoscaler decisions were unchanged in steady-state.
Elena Morales: I saw one flaky test fail in CI (streaming_e2e) — it timed out on the first run. Re-ran CI and it passed. Please add retry guard to that test.
Marcus Nguyen: Added retry+backoff to the e2e that retries warmup calls before asserting; added note in test comments.
Priya Shah: Approved after buffer bounds comment/override and adding the metric. Left a docs nit which is addressed.
release_notes:
- Improve streaming stability: smarter routing affinity and buffer/backpressure tuning
- Fix OpenAI-compat streaming for function/tool-calling and structured outputs (atomic frames + final delimiter)
- New observability: stream.proxy_chunk_retries, routing.stream_affinity_hit
- Config: routing.stream_affinity_enabled (off by default), PROXY_MAX_BUFFER_BYTES to cap memory usage
